paragraphs.text: Inspect, probe and manage MCP servers across every AI client on your machine — real handshake tests,
one settings page. A DeepSeek Harness plugin.
# MCP Manager
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that puts every MCP server definition on your machine in one place: it sca

ns the
config files of the clients you already use, normalises them, verifies that each server actua

lly answers the
MCP handshake, and keeps a small editable pool of its own.
Modelled on the idea of `dsh-skills-manager`, but for MCP servers instead of skills — and in English
ed on the idea of `dsh-skills-manager`, but for MCP servers instead of skills — and in English only.
Distributed as **`@zarpyk/dsh-mcp-manager`** (MIT). Source: <https://github.com/Zarpyk/dsh-mcp-manag
ributed as **`@zarpyk/dsh-mcp-manager`** (MIT). Source: <https://github.com/Zarpyk/dsh-mcp-manager>.
## What it does
- **Discovers** MCP servers from the config files of DeepSeek Harness, Claude Desktop / Claude Code,

Cursor,
VS Code, Windsurf, Codex, Zed, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cline, Roo Code, Kilo Code, Qwen, Trae

and more, both
user-level and per workspace.
- **Tests** any of them for real: it performs the MCP

`initialize` handshake and lists the tools the server
exposes, over stdio, streamable HTTP or legacy

SSE. Failures come with a plain-English hint
(missing executable, 401, DNS, certificate, timeout, u

nsupported protocol version).
- **Manages its own pool**: create, edit, enable/disable, soft-delete

to trash, restore and export servers.
- **Exposes tools to the agent, per chat**: `/mcp-<server>` tu

rns the bridge on for one conversation and
every tool that server publishes is registered there as `

mcp_<server>_<tool>`, callable directly — no
separate MCP connector plugin needed. A chat's own choi

ce always beats the pool-wide switch in
Settings → MCP Manager, so a server can be on everywhere and

off in one chat (or the other way round).
Sessions reopen automatically when the server changes and

follow `notifications/tools/list_changed`.
- **Stays visible even without tools**: an exposed serve

r that publishes nothing gets an `mcp_<server>_status`
placeholder tool, and a prompt-context line t

ells the model the MCP is connected but has no tools right now,
so a disconnected host app is never

mistaken for a missing server.
- **Exports** the pool as `mcpServers` JSON, VS Code `servers` JSON o

r Codex `config.toml`.
- **Imports** an existing config document by pasting it.
- **Never rewrites o

ther applications' files.** Discovered entries are strictly read-only; the pool lives in
the plugin'

' files.** Discovered entries are strictly read-only; the pool lives in
the plugin's own state file.

It also registers six agent tools so the model can inspect and maintain the same inventory:
`mcp_inv
entory`, `mcp_probe`, `mcp_save_server`, `mcp_expose_server`, `mcp_export_config`, `mcp_remove_serve
ory`, `mcp_probe`, `mcp_save_server`, `mcp_expose_server`, `mcp_export_config`, `mcp_remove_server`.
## Chat command
Exposure is **per chat**. Every pool server gets its own `/mcp-<server>` command, so the composer's
command palette completes the name for you, and the first run exposes that server in the chat where

te completes the name for you, and the first run exposes that server in the chat where you
typed it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`/mcp` stays available for the finer-grained verbs when you want them:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Local always wins: a choice made in a chat — either direction — beats the pool-wide switch in
**Sett
ings → MCP Manager**, and only affects that chat. Toggling a server on the settings page changes the
default for every chat that has not made its own choice. Hiding a pool-wide server in one chat leav

es it
available everywhere else.
Some servers — Unity's relay is the usual example — only publish tools while their host application

is
connected. While such a server is exposed and reports zero tools, the bridge re-reads its list ev

ery
15 seconds, so the tools appear on their own once the app connects; `/mcp refresh <name>` forces

that read
immediately. Until tools show up the server is still visible to the agent: the bridge reg

isters one
`mcp_<server>_status` placeholder tool for it (calling it re-reads the list and explains

what to do) and a
prompt-context line names the server, its transport and its current state, so the

model knows the MCP is
connected but has no tools instead of assuming it is missing.
The outcome renders in the conversation and never enters the model's context. Aliases: `ls`, `enable

`,
`disable`, `probe`, `reload`. Only the plugin's own pool can be exposed — discovered servers stay

read-only until you
copy them into the pool.
## Where it shows up
Two entry points, both disabled independently if their slot is unavailable:
- **Settings → MCP Manager** – a page in the settings dialog, next to the built-in sections (order 2

6).
- **Sidebar panel** – a server-bars icon in the sidebar (order 3) that opens the same page in th

e central
column. Pick it like any other panel; select another entry to leave.
[该节后续省略]
## Security notes
- Secrets in discovered configs are masked (`••••••` plus the last four characters) before they reac

h the
browser, except through the explicit `spec` action used to pre-fill the editor.
- Cross-origin

mutations are refused, and the custom header makes plain HTML form posts impossible.
- Probing a st

dio server executes its configured command. That is the same trust model as running the server
in it
s original client; only probe servers you would also run yourself.
## Limitations
- Tool exposure covers **pool** servers (the plugin's own store). Servers found in other clients' co

nfig files
stay read-only: use **Copy to pool** first, then expose them.
- Exposure supports stdio a

nd streamable HTTP servers. Legacy SSE endpoints can be probed but not exposed yet.
- Live tool refr

esh relies on `notifications/tools/list_changed`, which only flows on stdio; HTTP servers are
re-rea
d when you run `/mcp refresh <name>` (or reopen the page). Servers that publish no tools are polled

every 15 seconds while exposed.
- Project-level configs are only scanned for registered workspaces (

plus explicit ones passed by the UI).
- Per-chat overrides follow the chat session: a chat opened be

fore the override was set picks it up when it
starts its next step, and the override stays in `state

.json` for that session id.
- TOML support covers the subsets MCP clients actually write (tables, ar

rays, inline tables, dotted keys),
not the whole TOML 1.0 grammar.
